newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech authorities lift ban on gene maize imports.
newsitem.headline: Czech authorities lift ban on gene maize imports.

text.p: Czech authorities lifted a ban on imports of genetically manipulated feed maize on Friday after local tests proved it was safe, the Agriculture Ministry said.
The State Veterinary Administration halted the import of a 28,000-tonne consignment of maize last week after protests from environmental group Greenpeace.

The administration said in a statement that it had "on the basis of fine results of examination of samples of genetically manipulated maize imported by (Czech) Agropol Trading a.s. from the U.S., lifted a ban on imports of this kind of feed."
The European Commission on Wednesday followed the advice of its experts and approved the sale of gene-maize, defying protests by European environmentalists.
The ministry said on Friday that all further shipments of genetically altered maize into the Czech Republic would be subject to standard health safety controls.
The Czech Veterinary Administration had banned all use of gene-modified maize in the country until their tests had determined whether it was safe.
The Agriculture Ministry has asked the Czech Environment Ministry to include the European Union directive on handling genetically altered commodities in a draft law, and submit it to the cabinet.
Enviromentalists say the manipulated maize could reduce the efficacy of certain antibiotics.
The Czech office of Greenpeace said the ministry's decision proved nothing because there had not been a long-term study on the environmental and health risks of gene-altered organisms.
U.S. exporters do not separate the maize, developed by Swiss chemicals company Ciba Geigy AG and amounting to 0.5 to 0.6 percent of their crop, from conventional maize.
